clue.text: Control squeeze in scrum at game's end

indicators.note: the word squeeze is placed inside the word for a scrum, as the clue's preposition says

parts.note: a maul is a rugby scrum-like ruck around the ball carrier
to nip is to squeeze or pinch
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from game's

explanation.surface: A rugby coach wants control at the final scrum, squeezing in for the win.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate something is to handle or steer it skilfully, a synonym for controlling it.

clue.text: Horseless champion succeeded in love

indicators.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H, so being without it removes that letter

parts.note: a hero is a champion or defender
S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A champion jockey loses his mount but still wins in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H; taking it from HERO leaves ERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, so the name stands for love itself.

clue.text: Wild idea to correspond with hawk-headed god

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree or correspond with it
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: Someone has a crazy notion of matching an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful, impossible notion, a synonym for a wild idea or pipe dream.

clue.text: Recollected name? As one with this you may not

definitions.text: Recollected name? As one with this you may not

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered up again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether you could remember a name if you had memory loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Recollected splits as re-collected, the anagram signal; read whole, the clue says someone with this condition cannot recall things.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the condition in which you may not recollect things.

clue.text: Suggest enemy in opposition must cross river

indicators.note: to cross something here is to span it, so the enemy word lies over and around the river

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a shadow minister is the opposition party's counterpart to one in government

explanation.surface: Political commentary hinting that the rival party is about to ford a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the opposition party's front bench is the Shadow Cabinet, hence SHADOW for in opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to hint at or suggest something in advance.

clue.text: Digital feature starts with thesis on electronics

indicators.note: the starts of the three words that follow give their first letters

explanation.surface: An academic thesis on electronics with a digital topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Digital refers to digits, meaning fingers and toes, not computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is one of the digits of the foot, so it is a digital feature of the body.

clue.text: Reflective view supported by inventive personage

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-reversed, so the word for view is turned backwards

parts.note: a side of an argument is a point of view
on can mean resting upon, supported by something

explanation.surface: A mirrored view propped up by some creative figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor, so he is a very inventive personage.

clue.text: Shield of wood, old indeed, kept in historic island

indicators.note: the letters for old and indeed are held inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete is the Greek island of ancient Minoan history
so can mean indeed, as in 'it is so'

explanation.surface: An ancient wooden shield kept in a museum on a historic island.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tar oil painted on timber to preserve and protect it, a shield for wood.

clue.text: Last couple escapes death in Great Plague

indicators.note: the shortened word for death sits inside the word for great

parts.note: epic means great in scale

indicators.note: the final two letters of the word for death get away, so they are removed

parts.note: demise means death

explanation.surface: The final pair of victims escape death during the Great Plague of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last couple escapes' removes SE; 'Great Plague' looks like one phrase but splits into the container and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease, which a plague is.

clue.text: Letter to Greeks about time in disgrace

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes round the time abbreviation, as about can mean around

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone writes a letter to the Greeks about a time of shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: Hotel chain nabs houses

indicators.note: the phrase chain nabs contains, or houses, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A hotel chain buys up houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or pub offering lodging.

clue.text: Eco-politicians' electoral area? That's fresh turf

parts.note: the Greens are environmentalist political parties
a ward is a district electing a local councillor

explanation.surface: A local election district run by environmentalists is new political territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Turf suggests political territory, but here it means grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensward is an expanse of grassy turf, green and so fresh.

clue.text: Female bird I spotted in field

indicators.note: the bird and I are seen within the field, so they go inside its word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports seeing a small bird in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a woman's given name, so it is a female name.

clue.text: Convict in flat block worked land

indicators.note: the convict word is placed inside the word for a flat block

parts.note: a tile is a flat block of baked clay
a lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a block of flats once farmed the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat block' looks like a tower of flats but is a TILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is land that has been ploughed and cultivated for crops.

clue.text: Ultra-conservative parties

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration, and the plural gives two of them
a do is a party or celebration, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: Hard-line traditionalists holding their social gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo is slang for an old-fashioned person stuck in the past, an ultra-conservative.

clue.text: Crew member is as others taking order

indicators.note: the letters take on a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crew member, like everyone else, is waiting for instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: An air hostess is a member of an airliner's cabin crew.

clue.text: Miller's son gets great deal

definitions.meaning: ... the Miller's Son is one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws

explanation.definitionFit: Much is a great deal, and Much the Miller's Son is the merry man of the Robin Hood legend.

clue.text: Capital appearance, wearing new sash!

indicators.note: the letters for new and sash wear, or surround, the word for appearance

parts.note: an obi is a Japanese kimono sash
an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone shows up in the capital wearing a fresh sash.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Two-and-six in old money?

parts.note: two-and-six looks like half a crown in pre-decimal British coinage, but read as two plus six it makes a sum of old Spanish coins

explanation.walkthrough: Two-and-six (two shillings and sixpence) was half a crown in old British money; add the numbers instead and you have the old Spanish silver dollar of pirate tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were old Spanish silver coins, and two and six make eight.

clue.text: Turner embodies love and hate intensely

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within, so the turner surrounds the love letter

parts.note: a lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: The painter Turner captures both love and intense hatred in his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner, but it is a machine that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, the strongest sense of hating.

clue.text: Discuss without progress article Fox accepts for broadcast

indicators.note: the fox word takes in, or accepts, the article

parts.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters of for are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A Fox News article is accepted for broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges FOR to FRO; Fox looks like the TV network but is a tod.
explanation.definitionFit: To to-and-fro is to go back and forth in argument, discussing without getting anywhere.

clue.text: Dish is extravagant served in rhino's hide

indicators.note: the dish's ingredients are served inside the rhino's skin, so they go within it
the hide of the rhino is its outer skin, its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A lavish meal served inside a rhinoceros skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked in stock.

clue.text: One such as eats mice, scampering?

definitions.text: One such as eats mice, scampering?

indicators.note: scampering suggests running about wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cat scampers after mice, which it eats.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the animal while 'scampering' rearranges AS EATS MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siamese cat is a breed of domestic cat, an animal that eats mice.

clue.text: State uses wealth won unscrupulously

indicators.note: acting unscrupulously means crookedly, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A government uses ill-gotten riches.
explanation.definitionFit: New South Wales is a state of Australia.

clue.text: Scholarly monk departs after French town thrown into confusion

indicators.note: the departure letter comes after the town word

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was the scholarly Anglo-Saxon monk and historian
ville is French for town
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A learned monk leaves a French town in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedevilled means beset, tormented and thrown into confusion.

clue.text: Large repetition's not on for scholars

indicators.note: the word on is not present, so it is removed

parts.note: iteration is repetition
taken as written

explanation.surface: Large-scale repetition is no good for academics.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are learned, literary people, scholars.

clue.text: Huge collective sacks leaders, being provoked

indicators.note: sacking leaders removes the first letter of each word

parts.note: big means huge
united means joined together as a collective

explanation.surface: A large workers' collective fires its bosses after being stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacks leaders' takes the first letters, B and U, from BIG and UNITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignited means sparked off or roused, a figurative sense of being provoked.

clue.text: Appropriate key found by composer

indicators.note: the key letter is found beside, next to, the composer

parts.note: Sir Edward German was an English composer of light opera
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A composer finds a suitable key for a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent, a synonym for appropriate.

clue.text: Kidnapping sons as you'd expect

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
natch is slang for naturally, as you'd expect

explanation.surface: Kidnappers target someone's sons, as you would predict.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a kidnapping or abduction, as in a snatch squad.

clue.text: Northern runner appearing regularly in St Helens

indicators.note: every other letter of the following words appears, taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A northern athlete appears regularly at races in St Helens.
explanation.walkthrough: A runner in crosswords is often a river; the Tees flows through north-east England. St Helens is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in northern England, and a river runs.
